title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 44 (Nature of Shares or Debentures)

content.overview: Section 44 provides that the shares or debentures or other interest of any member in a company shall be movable property transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company.
content.glance: Shares, debentures and other member interests are movable property; transfer is in the manner provided by the articles.
content.study: The shares or debentures or other interest of any member in a company shall be movable property transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company. The section establishes legal character (movable property) and points transfer to the articles, read with the Act’s transfer provisions. Current-law framing: identify the interest; treat as movable property; apply articles and statutory transfer rules.

sections.heading: Movable property
sections.body: Shares, debentures or other interest of any member shall be movable property.

sections.heading: Transferability
sections.body: Transferable in the manner provided by the articles of the company (subject to the Act).

examples.title: Share as movable property
examples.body: A member’s share is movable property, but transfer still follows the articles and the Act.

hypotheticals.question: Does calling shares movable property make every transfer automatically effective against the company?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 44 characterises the property; transferability still follows the articles and the statutory transfer framework.

misconceptions.trap: Because shares are movable property, transfer formalities can be ignored.
misconceptions.correction: Section 44 links transfer to the manner provided by the articles; statutory transfer rules still apply.
